Each constant's name is the canonical region 23 * code as stored and returned (e.g. {@code "NSW"}). Regions are resolved from a single fixed 24 * city-to-region table ({@code Sydney -> NSW}, {@code Melbourne -> VIC}, {@code Brisbane -> QLD}); 25 * a city that is not in the table has no known region. 26 * 27 *

This is the one place the city-to-region mapping lives, so every rule that keys off an owner's 28 * region - such as the derived {@code locality} - resolves it identically. 29 */ 30 public enum Region { 31 32 NSW(2000, 2099), 33 VIC(3000, 3099), 34 QLD(4000, 4099); 35 36 private final int minPostcode; 37 38 private final int maxPostcode; 39 40 Region(int minPostcode, int maxPostcode) { 41 this.minPostcode = minPostcode; 42 this.maxPostcode = maxPostcode; 43 } 44 45 /** Fixed city -> region table; a city absent from this map has no known region. */ 46 private static final Map BY_CITY = Map.of( 47 "Sydney", NSW, 48 "Melbourne", VIC, 49 "Brisbane", QLD); 50 51 /** 52 * Reports whether the given 4-digit postcode falls within this region's inclusive postcode range 53 * (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). This is the one place the region-to-postcode 54 * range lives, so every rule that validates a postcode against an owner's region resolves it 55 * identically. 56 * 57 * @param postcode the numeric value of the owner's 4-digit postcode 58 * @return {@code true} when the postcode is within this region's range 59 */ 60 public boolean acceptsPostcode(int postcode) { 61 return postcode >= this.minPostcode && postcode <= this.maxPostcode; 62 } 63 64 /** 65 * Resolves the region for the given city from the fixed city-to-region table. 66 * 67 * @param city the owner's city, or {@code null} 68 * @return the matching region, or empty when the city is {@code null} or has no known region 69 */ 70 public static Optional forCity(String city) { 71 return city == null ? Optional.empty() : Optional.ofNullable(BY_CITY.get(city)); 72 } 73 } 74

`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class and both tests pass. The change is complete.

## Summary

The locality derivation now prefers the postcode over the city.

**`Region.java`** — Added a static `forPostcode(String)` method that parses the postcode and finds the region whose inclusive range contains it (reusing the existing `acceptsPostcode`), returning empty when the postcode is null, non-numeric, or in no known range.

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — Updated `locality(Owner)` to look up the region by postcode first, falling back to the city-to-region table only when the postcode doesn't resolve, then to `"UNKNOWN"`:

```java
return Region.forPostcode(owner.getPostcode())
    .or(() -> Region.forCity(owner.getCity()))
    .map(Region::name)
    .orElse("UNKNOWN");
```

This returns the same region for known cities (Sydney's 2000 → NSW) while disambiguating shared city names — a VIC-range postcode (3000) on an unknown city now yields VIC. Test suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 2/2 tests passing, including `coreRegionFromPostcodeRange` and `functionalityPostcodePreferredOverCity`).
